idle: Did I tell you about Wexford? And then I was in Fairhaven.
Suitcase is in the car. Just in case.
good_ice: Lovely ice! I've played on ice in nine cities and this is in the top nine.
bad_ice: Ice like this, I'd get traded off of.
wet_ice: A little damp. Like the airport in Kingsport at six in the morning.
hungry: I'll grab a hot dog. Never unpack on an empty stomach.
long_line: Long line. I've waited longer at baggage claim. Every time.
bored: If it's quiet, I start telling stories. You've been warned.
goal: Great goal! Somebody give that kid a standing ovation!
greet_owner: Hey! Good to see you! Still here! Haven't been traded!
leaving_happy: Leaving's my specialty. And I always come back.
leaving_angry: Well. I've been sent down from nicer places. Not many.

pro_practice: Dukes on the ice! I've been one seven times.
Head up, son! You'll be in Kingsport by Friday!
special: Standing ovation on the way in? I'll take one on the way out too.

first.say: Barry Pomeroy! Suitcase, to my friends, which is everyone. Nine GNHL clubs and the Duncannon Dukes seven times. You must be the owner. Great to be welcome!

options.text: Nine clubs? That's a lot of moving.

first_ovation.say: (He bows, deeply, then bows to the snack bar, then to the Zambelli.) Oh, you've done it now. I'll come every week.

first_suitcase.say: In the car. Packed. Nineteen years by the front door and I can't stop. The Hall of Honour has the old one. This is its little brother.

first_moving.say: Seven deadlines, three in a row, once in the airport. They traded me at gate twelve. I just went to gate fourteen.

options.text: Sorry, Suitcase. That's not how we treat a guest.

say: Dukes are out! I skate with them as the ambassador. Mostly I just say 'good job' and fall over.
Look at them go. Every one of them thinks he's going to Kingsport. Half of them will. Twice.
What can I tell you? I know nine cities.
Hey! Ask me anything. I'll tell you a story about it.
Fire away. And then I was in Fairhaven.

options.text: What do you like to watch?
How do you know Coach Rourke?
What do you think of the rink?
Any advice for a player my age?

job.say: I shake hands at the Frostbank, skate with the Dukes, and tell kids it's okay to get sent down. I got sent down seven times. Got a standing ovation every time.

say: Wexford, 1991. I scored on my own net, the crowd went wild, the coach shook my hand. And then I was in Fairhaven.
Northgate, 1994. Beautiful city. Lovely hotel. I unpacked one sock. And then I was in Fairhaven.
My last game, Fairhaven, 2004. We won the Cup. Teammates carried me round the ice. Nobody traded me. First time in nineteen years.

events.say: Dukes practice, because it's my job and I love it. The Old-timers', because they're my people. A bit of beer league, because I'm a defenceman and we never stop.

gossip.say: Annette played defence like she was angry at the puck personally. Now she coaches like she's angry at it professionally. Fairest coach I know. And Rejean won't let anyone touch his thermometer. Not even me. I tried once. I was in Fairhaven.

rink.say: This place? It's got bones. A good old barn with a dead spot in the boards and a crowd that knows your mother. That's all a rink needs.

options.text: And now it's fixed up a bit.

rink_better.say: New paint and the same crowd! That's the trick, and nobody gets it right. The Frostbank's got a video board the size of a barn. You've got a barn. I'd choose the barn.

path_player.say: Keep a bag by the door. Not because you'll leave. Because you'll want to know you could. Here. A Duncannon luggage tag. Put it on your hockey bag.

say: See you soon! Probably. You never know with me.
Off I go! Standing ovation optional. Encouraged.
